svg.title: Figure 4. What the model draws, and what steers
svg.desc: A synthetic view from the comma 3X road camera of a highway curve to the left (R = 514 m at 100 km/h) with the model's four lane lines, two road edges and the plan drawn as the onroad UI draws them, stamped for display, not for steering. Beside it: the steering command is one number, action[0,0] = 1.5 m/s² divided by v² to desiredCurvature = 0.00194 per metre. Lane lines and road edges are sampled at 33 distances up to 192 m, the plan at 33 times up to 10 s; the UI draws them to 100 m.
svg.text: Figure 4 · What the model draws, and what steers
The road camera with the model's lane lines, road edges and plan drawn the way the onroad UI draws them. None of it is the steering command.
Road camera of the comma 3X (1928×1208, f = 2648 px), level calibration, 1.22 m above the road.
Curve to the left, R = 514 m at 100 km/h (1.5 m/s², inside the ODD), three 3.7 m lanes. Beyond 100 m only the paint shows.
Synthetic drawing: the geometry a perfect model would report, with illustrative probabilities and stds; lane lines and edges drawn 3× the UI width.
One number, 20 times a second, to controlsd (Figure 2).
plan, laneLines, roadEdges, leads: to the UI, the logs
and drivingModelData. They steer only if the network
has no action head: then modeld derives the curvature
Spacing grows with distance: 0.19 m apart at first, 11.8 m at 192 m.
